ideas.title: Put it out with your beak
ideas.critique: This is the first post where the player acts on the fire instead of watching it. Water's latent heat and smothering by cutting off oxygen are real additions to fire.jl. The crisis loop could be replayed, and a filmed save next to a filmed loss is a new shape. The risk is that dousing becomes a scripted 'water hits fire, flame goes out' trigger. If the beak carrying and pushing isn't really simulated, it reads as one more campfire clip.

ideas.title: Read the heat by its colour
ideas.critique: Hot things glowing yellow, then orange, then red by Planck has already been posted twice, with the glass gather and the hot glass bubble. So the colour climbing is not news. What's new is a judgement skill with bellows and pulling the crucible out on cue. The malachite-to-copper switch at 1100 C is a threshold written in by hand unless the reduction chemistry is really modelled.

ideas.title: A wire that glows and melts
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
same_form: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: Joule heating with resistivity that depends on temperature, cooling, and melting is a core road step and real physics. But 'swap wires, watch thin glow and thick stay dark' is the side-by-side variants test the island keeps posting. It has a goal you can break, but little reason to play it twice on its own.

ideas.title: Charcoal from my own fire
ideas.critique: Pyrolysis where the air flux limits how fast wood turns to charcoal, with charcoal as a new material in the table, is a real step and a recipe players can discover. A time-lapse of a sand mound is thin to watch, though, and the payoff only lands once a kiln actually uses the fuel.

ideas.title: Smoke that drifts and tells
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: The island has never had a traced volume of smoke advected by wind and buoyancy, and that shows off the path tracer. Steam versus soot depending on how wet the wood is would be lovely. Friends coughing and moving is a scripted reaction on top. Choosing where to put the fire is a weak goal, and it does little for electricity.

ideas.title: Wet sand, dry sand
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: A moisture field driving both the material blend and how well sand sticks together touches many systems and would be a real rendering showcase, with the wet film shown as a clear coat. Sandcastles are only playable if sand building exists, though. Otherwise this is a still of a wet line.

ideas.title: A cell from two metals in brine
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
same_form: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: This is the core of the big goal: voltages from the galvanic series and internal resistance from the cell's geometry can be built on. The pitched film, a needle kicking in a shell watched by a fixed camera, is the island's most worn form. Bubbles and rust are probably just visual effects.

ideas.title: Cooking fish over coals
ideas.critique: Judging doneness from a real 1D heat conduction is a game loop people would replay, and friends reacting gives it warmth. It is a cooking minigame, a familiar genre. One fish shape with hard-coded browning thresholds puts it in the 'rig made for one case' category.

ideas.title: Fire spreads through the meadow
ideas.critique: A Rothermel spread model on a GPU grid, with firebreaks and the grass growing back, is a new playable system at island scale. A burnt-black front stopped at a wet strip is a striking shot. But a fire front driven by wind on a grid is a very familiar look from games, and it could tip into wrecking the island.

ideas.title: The glass bead from the beach
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Glass is already on the island, both blown and glowing. Making it from sand and soda ash is mostly a recipe label on something already posted. A dielectric bead in the sun repeats the recent glass stills.
